author: ValWood
body: My understanding is that TREX complex is pro-export. Its recruitment is coupled to correct processing events splicing, cap formation, proper 3′ end cleavage/polyadenylation. An mRNA that hasn't been processed correctly is less likely to have TREX (and therefore NXF1–NXT1) loaded onto it. So defective transcripts get excluded from export almost  as a side effect of never acquiring the full complex not because TREX detects and flags them. It is really licensing the export.  I might be wrong so I'll take a closer llook when I get chance. I haven't modelled this  pathway yet.
